calls.head: Toronto keeps shots outside; Montréal lets them in
calls.body: On quality allowed, Toronto sits 8th of 32, at the sheltered end of the scale. Montréal is 30th, at the exposed end.
calls.call: Toronto keeps the shots it allows further from danger than Montréal does.

calls.head: Montréal locks it down; Toronto doesn’t
calls.body: Montréal ranks 17th of 32 for shot suppression, toward the stingy end; Toronto ranks 32nd, toward the porous end.
calls.call: Montréal allows fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than Toronto.

calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Montréal had 48.0 per 60 and Toronto 53.9 per 60. Coming in, Montréal was at 57.3 per 60 and Toronto at 63.6 per 60.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 36% chance, and it went the way we feared.

MTL.head: We gave Montréal a 64% chance, and Montréal delivered.

surprises.head: Montréal tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Texier, K. Dach, P. Danault played 9:22 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Montréal’s usual lines.
